stories.new_fact: AP reported a federal judge ordered the White House to restore access for reporters from CNN, Politico, The Hill and MS NOW while their lawsuit continues.
stories.new_takeaway: The issue has moved from outlet-specific denials to a court-tested question about whether neutral logistics rules become viewpoint discrimination.
stories.why_now: The order was issued Monday, September 21, and changes today's access posture.
stories.previous_coverage: September 20 covered initial denials; today's development has a new court order and a different takeaway focused on temporary legal relief.
stories.uncertainty: The underlying lawsuit is unresolved; appeal, policy rewrite or compliance posture are not yet known.
stories.watch: White House appeal, revised credential rules, or restored access while the case proceeds.

stories.new_fact: Axios reported Mayor Andrew Ginther's 2026 budget plan would use $25 million from Columbus's rainy-day fund to help balance operations.
stories.new_takeaway: Reserve use becomes a budget-discipline test: one-time money can smooth a year, but not fix a recurring cost and revenue mismatch.
stories.why_now: The 2026 budget proposal was reported Monday and heads into local scrutiny.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior seven-episode coverage of Columbus reserve-fund pressure; recent local stories covered schools, civic facilities and Grove City development consent.
stories.uncertainty: The final council budget, remaining reserve balance and recurring spending choices are not yet settled.
stories.watch: Budget hearings showing whether reserve use is paired with recurring cost, revenue or service-level decisions.

stories.new_fact: Fannie Mae Multifamily Lender Letter 25-12 makes updated loan documents applicable to new multifamily commitments issued on or after September 22, 2026.
stories.new_takeaway: The affected workflow is legal-document selection and closing-package control for multifamily loans, not consumer rate shopping.
stories.why_now: The effective date is today, September 22.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent lending segments covered UAD appraisal delivery, PMI outreach, MGIC limits, VantageScore and rates; none covered multifamily loan documents.
stories.uncertainty: Borrower counsel, lender systems and closing teams may apply the date gate differently until internal instructions are tested.
stories.watch: Whether lenders publish clean commitment-date gates and closing-package instructions for new multifamily commitments.

stories.new_fact: Mastercard and Danske Bank said they completed Denmark's first payment where an AI agent made the purchase and payment on behalf of a consumer, using Mastercard Agent Pay.
stories.new_takeaway: Agentic payments move the banking-AI question from assistant output to authorization, issuer signals, authentication and dispute proof.
stories.why_now: The transaction announcement was dated September 21.
stories.previous_coverage: September 19 covered Mastercard and Alchemy's broader agentic commerce deal; this is a named bank demonstration with a completed transaction.
stories.uncertainty: No adoption, fraud, dispute, customer-satisfaction or error-rate metric was disclosed.
stories.watch: Named issuer metrics on agent-authorized payment attempts, declines, mistaken purchases, disputes or customer-service volume.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Added Danske Bank / Mastercard Agent Pay for consumer-authorized AI-agent purchase and payment; lane 1/8 payments and controls; announced; evidence company claim plus trade reporting; no performance metric disclosed.

stories.new_fact: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.7, made it available on the xAI API, and documented a U.S. regional endpoint with a 10 percent premium plus a fast variant billed at twice standard token rates in limited channels.
stories.new_takeaway: The frontier workflow implication is model routing for coding agents: access, region, token economics and long-task reliability matter as much as headline benchmark scores.
stories.why_now: The release and docs were dated September 21.
stories.previous_coverage: No prior seven-episode coverage of Grok 4.7; recent frontier stories covered U.S.-China governance, slowdown litigation and AI self-improvement metrics.
stories.uncertainty: Benchmarks are lab-reported; independent replication and real cost per completed coding task remain unknown.
stories.watch: Independent coding-agent evaluations and customer reports on task completion cost versus Grok 4.6, GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Fable 5.1.
stories.frontier_bar: Price or access shift plus agent and tool-use advance; a new model release with API access, regional endpoint and coding-agent positioning.

stories.new_fact: Early ETF screens showed QQQ modestly higher, SPY near flat and TLT still central to the long-rate watch.
stories.new_takeaway: Tech resilience does not by itself relieve borrowers if long bonds remain weak.
stories.why_now: Market context was checked before drafting on September 22.
stories.previous_coverage: Markets are covered compactly each day; today's angle stays short and updates the financing-stress screen.
stories.uncertainty: ETF prices and direction change through the trading day.
stories.watch: Whether TLT stabilizes and broader indexes join any AI-linked strength.

stories.new_fact: The National Weather Service forecast for the Ohio State University Airport area called for cloudy skies Tuesday, a high near 67, a 50 percent shower chance Tuesday night and showers likely Wednesday.
stories.new_takeaway: The useful local weather advice is less about severe weather and more about damp commutes, slow-drying fields and outdoor backups.
stories.why_now: Weather affects today's Columbus commute and planning.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine daily weather, not a repeated full story.
stories.uncertainty: Shower timing and local totals can change with later forecast updates.
stories.watch: Overnight showers and Wednesday morning wet-road timing.
